newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends firm, meal mixed on spread action.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends firm, meal mixed on spread action.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed firmer while soymeal ended mixed on small-lot oil/meal spread trading, floor sources said.
Both markets drew strength late from a rally in corn which spilled over into beans.
Commercial buying on the breaks limited losses in soymeal. Traders said Cargill Inc bought 250 lots May soymeal and 200 lots July. Iowa Grain reportedly bought 150 July.
Soyoil found support amid talk it was undervalued relative to world palm oil prices and there was talk of improved export business as buyers took advantage of that.
Malaysian FOB RBD palm oil on Monday was at $560 per tonne for February delivery. U.S. crude degummed soybean oil was at $537 per tonne for February delivery, export sources said.
Korea tendered Monday for 44,500 tonnes soymeal but talk the purchases would be made from India cut gains.
Traders also cited speculation that China would resell soymeal. China reportedly has large stockpiles of soymeal clogging ports and could sell at a substantial profit.
Soyoil ended 0.16 to 0.11 cent per lb higher with March up 0.15 at 24.36 cents. Soymeal closed $0.80 per ton lower to $0.50 higher with March unchanged at $238.10.
On the day, ADM sold 50 lots March soyoil and 250 lots May. Term Commodities bought 200 March, traders said.
Soyoil volume was estimated by CBOT at 10,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 7,686 lots. Soymeal volume was pegged at 18,000 lots, against Friday's tally of 14,258 lots, CBOT said.
